text:
Anya V: Heads up — noticed a regression on canary after yesterday's runtime driver rollout. Kernel selection frequency changed and tail latency for seq bin 129-256 jumped ~50%. Repro and quick notes below.

Mike L: ugh, when did the driver rollout land? link to deploy? :eyes:

InfraBot: deploy/redwood-runtime-driver v2.14.0 -> canary started at 2026-02-18T09:04:12Z (build b7f3c).

Anya V: repro steps: send same traffic from perf harness v2 that pins model=x-large@v3, seqlen dist focused at 160 avg. Observed: most requests went to kernel=fused_gemm_v2 (expected), but a subset got kernel=matmul_direct which is ~2x slower at our microbatch sizes. Logs: 
```
[2026-02-18T09:12:21Z] req=abcd1234 seqbin=129-256 kernel_choice=fallback:matmul_direct latency=18.9ms
[2026-02-18T09:12:21Z] req=abcd1256 seqbin=129-256 kernel_choice=preferred:fused_gemm_v2 latency=10.2ms
[2026-02-18T09:12:22Z] kernel_picker: seqbin=129 heuristics_score={mem:0.3,lat:0.8,arch_pref:0.0} -> pick=matmul_direct
```

Sophia K: I ran a quick perf profile and uploaded a flamegraph: https://perf.redwood.corp/graphs/canary-3265432199-flame.svg :fire: The hotspots are in kernel selection decision path (timer + fallback) and not the kernels themselves — seems we hit a path where arch_pref is zeroed.

Tom H: could be key provenance — autotuner may be using stale telemetry for that cohort after the driver id changed. We had a regression earlier where persistent KV entries missed the new driver-gen header.

Priya R: do we have cache keys including driver-gen and model-hash? I thought we included model version only. If driver-gen isn't part of the key, cache can return picks computed under previous driver heuristics.

Anya V: confirmed: kv key pattern is `kernel_hint:{model}:{seqbin}`. No driver-gen or driver-config-hash. So stale hints can survive runtime swap or driver rollback.

Mike L: that would explain it. When driver rolled, autotuner on some nodes wrote hints under same key but with different interpretation. nodes reading those hints after new driver saw misleading values.

Sophia K: quick experiment: invalidating keys for model=x-large removed the slow pickups and latency dropped back to expected. I ran a canary with `redis-cli EVAL` quick delete for `kernel_hint:x-large:*` and metrics recovered.

Tom H: temporary mitigation = purge keys on rollout. Long term = include driver-gen and model binary hash in key namespace, or store key provenance (driver-gen, kernel-picker-version, timestamp) inline with the hint.

Priya R: prefer provenance field + TTL. That way we can avoid full namespace purge and also decide on compatibility rules (accept hints if driver-gen matches or if hint_ts < X). Also allow backfill transforms if we add salting later.

Mike L: any perf cost of adding driver-gen to key? Slightly larger key sizes, but negligible. Persisting provenance as value blob increases size a bit. Tradeoffs: reading extra blob vs simpler key names.

Anya V: decision proposal: 1) emergency: add preflight hook to rollout that runs targeted purge for known models on canary and prod for next deploy (owner: Tom). 2) short-term patch: accept provenance in value and check driver-gen on read; if mismatch treat as miss (owner: Priya). 3) long-term: salt key with driver-gen and model-hash for deterministic partitioning + TTL + optional compatibility map for driver skew (owner: Sophia). Rollout window: emergency purge immediate, short-term patch within 48h, long-term design RFC in 2 weeks.

Tom H: I can run the purge now on canary and roll to prod purge after approval. Command used: `redis-cli --scan --pattern 'kernel_hint:x-large:*' | xargs -r redis-cli del` (will coordinate with infra window).

Priya R: I'll open a small PR that changes read path to check `value.meta.driver_gen` vs current runtime driver id and return miss if mismatch + add provenance schema. Tests and canary tomorrow.

Sophia K: I'll draft the RFC for key salting + backward compatibility. Will include benchmark sims for heatmap of memory overhead (estimated +10%) and effect on lookups.

Mike L: add metric we can watch: `runtime.kv.hint.provenance_mismatch{model}` and `runtime.kernel_pick.stale_hits` and tag by seqbin. We'll set alerts if stale_hits > 0.5% for customer traffic.

Anya V: thanks everyone. Action items: Tom (purge canary + prod purge schedule), Priya (provenance read patch PR), Sophia (RFC + benchmarks), Mike (alert + dashboard). Reopen here with links to PRs and perf graphs. :thumbsup:
